title: A scheme unramified over a field is discrete
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be an unramified morphism [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then the underlying topological space of $Y$ is discrete: every point $y\in Y$ is open in $Y$ (so every subset of $Y$ is open, and every point of $Y$ is also closed). (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), part (1), direction "only if", topological part; Stacks proves it from Morphisms, Lemma 02V5 (unramified implies locally quasi-finite) and Morphisms, Lemma 01TH (a point at which a morphism locally of finite type is quasi-finite is isolated in its fibre); Algebra, Lemma 00UW (residue fields finite separable) is used only for the other parts of 02G7 (1).)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field), statement part (1) and proof, lines 7790-7826

proof.text: For any affine opens U of Spec k and V of Y with V contained in the inverse image of U, equip the section-ring map g.appLE U V e with its induced algebra structure. Scheme.Hom.finiteType_appLE gives Algebra.FiniteType on the section rings. The Mathlib instance from the open diagonal gives FormallyUnramified g, and Scheme.Hom.formallyUnramified_appLE gives Algebra.FormallyUnramified on the same section rings.

The instance in Mathlib.RingTheory.Unramified.LocalStructure (lines 329-332) gives Algebra.QuasiFinite for every finite-type formally unramified algebra. This is definitionally the RingHom.QuasiFinite property of the section-ring map. Package these maps in Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite g. This directly uses Mathlib quasi-finiteness, without the project predicate or its comparison theorem.

A field is Artinian, so Mathlib makes Spec k locally Artinian. Apply AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyArtinian.of_locallyQuasiFinite g (Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiFinite, lines 147-163) to obtain IsLocallyArtinian Y. Apply the instance AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyArtinian.discreteTopology (Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Artinian, lines 94-103) to conclude DiscreteTopology Y. This also implies that every singleton is open and closed, as in the unchanged node statement.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks Morphisms 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field, line 7790) proof of (1), 02V5 (lemma-unramified-quasi-finite, line 7779, proof = Algebra 02UR line 41599), 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, line 3664) and Definition 01TD (line 3538); all tags verified in tags/tags. Statement kept; only its parenthetical source remark corrected: Algebra 00UW (residue fields finite separable) is not used for the topological part. Proof in three steps following Stacks: unramified => quasi-finite at every point (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points, 02V5), quasi-finite at a point of a locally finite type morphism => isolated in the fibre (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated, 01TH (1)=>(2)), the fibre over the single point of Spec k being Y itself, and the elementary passage to discreteness and closedness. Quasi-finiteness is the existing definition pqf-def-quasifinite (Stacks 01TD). The route via lem-weil-pbc-unramified-algebra-over-field-product was not taken: that node is 02G7(1) in the affine case, whose Stacks proof itself passes through the discreteness proved here, so citing it would risk a cycle. Mathlib: no scheme-level FormallyUnramified -> LocallyQuasiFinite; Mathlib's quasi-finiteness (Algebra.QuasiFinite, Scheme.Hom.QuasiFiniteAt) differs from Stacks' by a theorem, so neither new node is a leaf; candidate Scheme.Hom.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_asFiber recorded.

Correct. Worker corrected the parenthetical source remark in the statement (00UW is not used for discreteness); content unchanged. Stage-3 note: pqf-def-quasifinite is still imported.
